summary.description: First sentence: what changed, for a developer; it becomes the pull request title (no issue number, nothing secret). More sentences if needed: where the code differed from the issue, what was declined and why

plain.description: For people who do not read code; shown at the top of the pull request. Plain words: no file names, function names, commands or backticks

what.description: What this pull request does, as a user would see it; two or three sentences

decided_myself.description: Everything the issue did not say and you decided yourself, one sentence each; empty list if none. Leave nothing out: the reviewer compares it with the diff

risk.description: If the change is wrong: what a user would see and how to go back

verify.description: How a person checks it: where to go, what to do, what they should see

files.description: One entry per file changed, created or deleted (in a rework: for the whole pull request)

why.description: Why this file had to change

red.description: The new test failing before the change

command.description: The exact command that was run; empty string if no test could be written

output.description: The lines of its output that matter, verbatim (failing test name, expected, actual). If no test could be written: why not, and how the starting point was confirmed

green.description: The same test passing after the change

command.description: The exact command that was run

checks.description: Every configured check and every other test command that was run

ok.description: true only if it was actually run and passed

not_verified.description: Everything that was not run or not verified, one item each, in plain words; also flaws seen nearby and left alone (start those with "Not fixed here:"). Empty list only if everything claimed was run and seen

cannot_fix.description: Only when the work was not done: it cannot be done, is intended behaviour, or is already done on the base branch. Leave it out otherwise

reason.description: Why, what was found, and what should change (for "already done": the commits that did it)
